# InkFrame for Immich

> InkFrame is a free, open-source (MIT) photo frame that shows one well-chosen photo every few days from your own Immich library on a battery-powered 7.5-inch e-paper panel, the Seeed Studio XIAO 7.5" ePaper Panel. A small server (the renderer, a Docker container) picks a landscape photograph, crops it to 800x480, tones and dithers it to one bit, and serves the finished frame. The panel's firmware (ESPHome) wakes, fetches, draws and sleeps. A Home Assistant integration (HACS custom repository, domain `inkframe`) chooses where photos come from and shows what is on the glass and what is waiting.

Key facts:

- Tested hardware: Seeed Studio XIAO 7.5" ePaper Panel (ESP32-C3, UC8179 controller, 800x480, black and white). Other e-paper panels are unverified; colour and greyscale panels are not supported.
- Why a server: the ESP32-C3 has no PSRAM and about 200 KB of heap, so it cannot fetch, decode, scale or dither a photograph. The server sends a finished one-bit frame of 48,000 bytes that the panel only copies to the display.
- Photo choice: landscape by EXIF orientation (not by width and height), taken by a camera (EXIF make present), scored for texture (mean absolute Laplacian); of twenty candidates, a random one under the busyness cap is rendered, or the calmest when none is. Portraits are cropped around the faces Immich found, or skipped if you prefer.
- Sources, chosen from Home Assistant: random, recent (last N days), people (any of those ticked), one person, an album, or a text search such as "cat".
- Cadence: By default the renderer draws a new photo every 3 days at 07:00 (Photo every and Photo hour). With the default Sleep interval of 168 h the panel wakes on those mornings only. A shorter Sleep interval adds checks on a fixed clock grid anchored on the draw hour: 6 h gives 01:00, 07:00, 13:00 and 19:00. A check takes about 7 seconds awake and a draw about 35.
- Waking: the panel cannot be woken from the network. A change made in Home Assistant reaches the glass at the panel's next wake. Pressing the reset button on the panel wakes it at once.
- Rendered is not displayed: the `On panel` sensor turns true only after the panel sends an authenticated acknowledgement following a successful draw.
- Privacy: the renderer reads your Immich server and talks to nothing else. Every endpoint except `/healthz` needs a shared bearer token. Traffic is plain HTTP, so keep it on a trusted network.
- Requirements: an Immich server and API key (asset.read, asset.view, asset.statistics, album.read, person.read), a host with Docker for the renderer, Home Assistant 2025.1.0 or newer (declared minimum; exercised on 2026.9.4), ESPHome to flash the panel.
- Install: run the renderer with `docker compose up -d` in `server/`, flash `firmware/immich-frame.yaml` with ESPHome, then add `https://github.com/CaputoDavide93/InkFrame-Immich` to HACS as a custom repository of type Integration and add the integration in Home Assistant.
- Trade-off: the panel sleeps for days, so changes are not instant, and the renderer must run all the time next to Immich.
- Independent project, not affiliated with or endorsed by Seeed Studio or Immich.
